findings.title: NPE when the all-clients resource is missing
findings.body: In hasPermission(client, scope), when no per-client resource exists the code calls getResourceTypeResource(...). That method returns null if the schema is not supported or the resource is not found. The result is passed directly to policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) and later to resource.getScopes(), with no null check. If the 'Clients' resource is absent, for example in a realm created before the schema change, every client permission check throws an NPE instead of returning false.

findings.title: Per-client lookup falls back to all-clients without merging
findings.body: When a per-client resource exists, only that resource is evaluated and the all-clients permission is not consulted. A client with a permission for one scope, for example VIEW, will then be denied MANAGE even if an all-clients MANAGE permission exists. The user-type tests rely on fallback to the all-users permission, so this behavior is inconsistent with them.

findings.title: Listener gated on the V1 feature flag
findings.body: The cleanup listener is now wrapped in Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) (V1). It previously ran unconditionally. When only V1 is disabled, which is the V2 case, role, client and group removal no longer clears permissions. The listener also calls setPermissionsEnabled, which now throws UnsupportedOperationException in ClientPermissionsV2. The gate only works by accident.

findings.title: canManage() calls super and the V2 override
findings.body: canManage() delegates to super.canManage(). If super.canManage() calls other overridable methods, it may behave unexpectedly. The name-based hasPermission(scope) also looks up the 'Clients' resource by name, which differs from the type-based lookup in the other overload.
